clue.text: Bob cuts leaves back under pressure

indicators.note: the shilling slices into the reversed verb, sitting inside it
back tells us the synonym for leaves is read from end to start

parts.note: to leave a place is to desert it, so leaves gives deserts
a bob was an old British shilling, abbreviated S

explanation.surface: A hairdresser trims the foliage while feeling the strain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like a haircut but is a shilling, S. 'back' turns DESERTS into STRESED, and 'cuts' puts the S inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone stressed is strained and anxious, which is what being under pressure means.

clue.text: Hardy girl takes a long time to find password

parts.note: Tess of the d'Urbervilles is the heroine of Thomas Hardy's novel
an era is a long period of history

explanation.surface: A Thomas Hardy heroine spends ages trying to recall a secret word.
explanation.walkthrough: TESS is Hardy's Tess of the d'Urbervilles, a novel well known in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Rome a tessera was a small tablet bearing a watchword passed among soldiers, hence a password.

clue.text: General deployed soldiers close to target — it's blown up

indicators.note: troops deployed are rearranged into new positions, so the letters of General are reshuffled

parts.note: soldiers are men in the ranks

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A general sends his troops near a target, which is then destroyed by explosives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deployed' rearranges GENERAL into ENLARGE; 'close to' takes T from target.
explanation.definitionFit: A photographic print made larger than its negative is said to be blown up.

clue.text: Knockout in South Carolina boxing ring followed by knockout

indicators.note: followed by sets the second abbreviation after the first group
boxing means enclosing, so the state abbreviation surrounds the ring

parts.note: SC is the postal abbreviation for South Carolina
a ring is round like the letter O
KO is the standard boxing abbreviation for a knockout

explanation.surface: A boxing knockout in a South Carolina ring is followed by another knockout.
explanation.definitionFit: Socko is American slang for something stunningly impressive, just as a knockout is a sensation.

clue.text: Indicated what's needed to get code from coed?

parts.note: the word code ends in the letters D then E, which is what must be written
getting one thing from another means leaving the second behind, so here it stands for not
the word coed ends in the pair E then D, the order that must be given up

explanation.surface: A puzzle question asks how to turn one short word into another.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue implies 'DE, NOT ED': swapping the final ED of COED for DE gives CODE, so 'from' does the work of NOT.
explanation.definitionFit: To denote something is to signify or point it out, so denoted means signified.

clue.text: One's impressed by padre changing nappy

indicators.note: pressed into, so the numeral sits inside the rearranged priest
changing means altering the order of the letters of padre

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone is impressed watching a priest change a baby's nappy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' turns PADRE into DAPER, and 'impressed by' puts I inside it. Diaper is the American word for a nappy.
explanation.definitionFit: Diaper is the American term for the absorbent cloth or pad a baby wears, which Britons call a nappy.

clue.text: Sloth for one is extremely sedate and idly disposed

indicators.note: disposed in the sense of arranged, so these letters are set out afresh
the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sloth is described as very calm and lazily inclined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' gives SE from sedate; 'disposed' rearranges SE, AND and IDLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloth, meaning laziness, is one of the seven cardinal vices of Christian teaching.

clue.text: Immediately save old woman

indicators.note: save means except, so the old letter is left out

parts.note: anon is an old word for at once or immediately

explanation.surface: An urgent instruction to rescue an elderly lady straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'save' means except: ANON without O.
explanation.definitionFit: Ann is a common female first name, and crosswords often clue girls' names with a word for female.

clue.text: Back 'Arry's filly perhaps after tip

indicators.note: after puts the dropped-letter animal behind the tip word

parts.note: the tip of something is its end

indicators.note: 'Arry is a Cockney who drops his H, so his version of a word loses its H

parts.note: a filly is a young female horse, an example of the animal

explanation.surface: A Cockney punter backs his horse after receiving a racing tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arry stands for a Cockney (working-class Londoner), who drops initial H, making HORSE into 'ORSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To back a plan or candidate is to support it publicly, the same as endorsing it.

clue.text: Independent's description of damsel flirting?

parts.note: the words damsel flirting have the letters S, E, L, F running across them, so a self lies within them

explanation.surface: A newspaper describes a young woman flirting, perhaps as reserved.
explanation.walkthrough: The Independent is also the newspaper running this crossword. In 'damSEL Flirting' a SELF is held inside the words.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone or something needing nothing from outside is independent, complete within itself.

clue.text: Oddball hitched around Ireland, having nothing

indicators.note: having joins the zero onto the end
the married word goes around the abbreviation for Ireland

parts.note: getting hitched is slang for marrying, so wed
nothing is zero, shaped like O

explanation.surface: An eccentric hitchhiked around Ireland with no money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hitched' suggests hitchhiking, but here it is getting hitched, i.e. marrying.
explanation.definitionFit: A weirdo is an eccentric person, someone odd, exactly what an oddball is.

clue.text: Skiing manoeuvre set standard

parts.note: a television set is informally a tele or telly
a mark is a standard or level to reach, as in up to the mark

explanation.surface: A skiing move is fixed as the benchmark technique.
explanation.definitionFit: The telemark is a turn in skiing, with one ski advanced and the knee bent, named after a Norwegian region.

clue.text: Setting cryptic in essence occupies Klingsor

indicators.note: the jumbled phrase takes up the space inside the setter's pronoun

parts.note: Klingsor is the setter of this puzzle, so from his point of view he is me

indicators.note: cryptic means puzzling or obscure, so the letters of in essence are jumbled

explanation.surface: A setter explains that puzzle-making is essentially his whole occupation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cryptic' jumbles IN ESSENCE into ISEENSCEN, which 'occupies' ME, the setter Klingsor.
explanation.definitionFit: Mise-en-scene is the arrangement of scenery and props on stage or film, that is, the setting.

clue.text: Mother's done OK, somehow getting borders for dresses to be all the same

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother

indicators.note: somehow says the letters of done OK end up arranged in some way
the borders of a word are its outside letters

explanation.surface: Mum has managed fine making trimmed edges for frocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges DONE OK into KENOOD; 'borders for' takes DS from dresses.
explanation.definitionFit: If something makes no odds it makes no difference, so the choices are equal.

clue.text: Ended row about book with daughter, having taken the plunge?

parts.note: something that has ended is over

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the book and daughter letters flank the rowing word

parts.note: to row is to oar a boat

explanation.surface: A row ends with a daughter and a book, after someone has finally taken a big step.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' sets B and D around OAR to make BOARD. The definition is playful: going over the side of a ship is literally taking the plunge.
explanation.definitionFit: Going over the side of a ship into the water is a literal plunge, punning on making a bold decision.

clue.text: Staunch supporter

definitions.meaning: to staunch a flow of blood is to stop or ... it
the stalk that holds up a flower or leaf

explanation.surface: A loyal fan is described as unwavering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staunch' reads as the adjective loyal, but it is the verb meaning stop a flow.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb for checking a flow, and a noun for the stalk bearing up a plant's flower.

clue.text: Teenage problem embraced by Isaac Newton

indicators.note: the letters are held within the run of the scientist's name

explanation.surface: Even the young Isaac Newton suffered adolescent troubles.
explanation.definitionFit: Spots and pimples are a common skin complaint among adolescents.

clue.text: Maybe Finn fruitlessly supports college for a laugh

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting part is below, so the trimmed name sits under the college letter
without its fruit, so the berry is removed from the name

parts.note: Huckleberry Finn is Mark Twain's boy hero, so Finn may be Huckleberry

explanation.surface: A Finnish student, deprived of fruit, holds up his college for amusement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finn' suggests a person from Finland but is Huckleberry Finn; 'fruitlessly' drops BERRY to leave HUCKLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A chuckle is a quiet, suppressed laugh.

clue.text: Stop getting furious like a Siberian tiger!

parts.note: to stop something is to end it
someone who gets furious is angered

explanation.surface: An instruction not to provoke a big cat into rage.
explanation.definitionFit: The Siberian tiger is a threatened species at risk of extinction, a classic example.

clue.text: Having Rasta hairstyle is terrifying

definitions.meaning: wearing dreadlocks, the matted locks associated with Rastafarians

explanation.surface: A Rastafarian's hairdo is called frightening.
explanation.definitionFit: Wearing dreadlocks, and greatly feared, as in a much-feared outcome.

clue.text: Plant disease especially found in small island

indicators.note: the abbreviation turns up inside the small island word

parts.note: an eyot is a small island in a river

explanation.surface: A plant blight is found mostly on a tiny island.
explanation.walkthrough: EYOT (also ait) is a small river island, chiefly British, especially on the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyespot is a fungal infection of cereals and other crops, marked by eye-shaped lesions.

clue.text: Durable clothes you said? I'll go in for fitting

indicators.note: clothes as a verb means covers or wraps, so the steady word wraps the letter

parts.note: something durable is stable and lasting

indicators.note: go in says the letter from I'll joins the sounded letter inside the steady word
said means spoken, and the word you spoken is the letter U

parts.note: the word you sounds like the letter U
I'll is I will, so I is the letter that will go in

explanation.surface: Someone tells you to wear hard-wearing clothes while they try them on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' puts U, which sounds like 'you' when 'said', inside STABLE; then I 'go in' too.
explanation.definitionFit: Something suitable is appropriate or apt, a synonym of fitting.

clue.text: General Assembly's first cut by 90%

indicators.note: the first letter, the Roman thousand, is reduced by nine tenths to the Roman hundred

parts.note: a muster is an assembly of troops

explanation.surface: A legislature's leading figure suffers a drastic cut.
explanation.walkthrough: M is the Roman numeral 1000; cutting it by 90% leaves 100, C.
explanation.definitionFit: George Armstrong Custer was a US cavalry general, killed at Little Bighorn.

clue.text: Change sides in insensitive style

indicators.note: the sides are right and left, so the R for right becomes L for left

parts.note: crass means tactless and insensitive

explanation.surface: Someone who switches political sides has a tactless manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Class here means elegance or stylishness, as when someone has real class.

clue.text: Unruly as kids, initially needing slap to stop fighting

indicators.note: unruly means disorderly, so these letters are thrown out of order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of needing

parts.note: slap is theatrical slang for greasepaint or cosmetics

explanation.surface: Like squabbling children, they need a smack to stop them fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slap' looks like a smack but is slang for cosmetics. 'Unruly' rearranges AS KIDS plus N into KISSAND.
explanation.definitionFit: To kiss and make up is an idiom for reconciling after a quarrel.

clue.text: First of seasons each year is spring

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of seasons

parts.note: p.a. stands for per annum, Latin for each year

explanation.surface: The first season of every year is spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' looks like the season but is a mineral spring.
explanation.definitionFit: A spa is a mineral spring, or the resort built around one.

clue.text: Relief after agent returned

indicators.note: after places the help word behind the agent

parts.note: a sales agent is a rep, short for representative
relief given to the needy is aid

explanation.surface: Someone felt relief once their agent came back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' looks like a reversal signal, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To return money owed is to pay it back, so returned means repaid.

clue.text: Fancy dress set for Charlotte and Madeleine?

indicators.note: fancy as in fancy dress, here read as elaborate rearrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: A fancy-dress outfit is made for two girls named Charlotte and Madeleine.
explanation.walkthrough: Charlotte and Madeleine look like girls' names but are a fruit pudding and a small sponge cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A charlotte is a baked fruit pudding and a madeleine a small sponge cake; both are sweet courses.
